gap: No result ChatGPT got states a sound-meter reading for a Hall effect keyboard: the one open figure is Hardware Busters' 55.1 dBA average (69.9 dBA spacebar peak, 31.9 dBA room, meter at 10 cm) for the stock-switch Epomaker HE75 V2, and no lab figure could be opened for any silent-switch board, including the Gamakay TK75HE V2 with Phoenix switches.
standout_why: I compared against hlplanet's guide (cited), RTINGS' best quiet list (cited), thegadgetverse, mechvibes and torontokeyboardman. None gives a dBA figure for a Hall effect board; RTINGS quotes one figure, 47.6 dBA, and it is for the mechanical NuPhy Air75 V3. But thegadgetverse (rank 4 in the second chat, not cited) already says 'No lab has published a numeric score for any dedicated silent HE switch', so the absence itself is not new. Only the Hardware Busters baseline for a non-silent magnetic board is new, and it is not for a candidate. Not compared: dopyoe (cited; certificate error), the two cited Reddit threads, mechanicalkeyboard.net, geekgamingtricks, keyboardverdict, bygrinstow and both PC Gamer lists, none of which I opened.
decides: It does not change the pick. No meter reading ranks the Gamakay TK75HE V2 (Phoenix) against the NuPhy Air75 HE or Wooting 80HE, so the Gamakay pick rests on switch design and on named listeners: AppleInsider's Wesley Hilliard tested the Phoenix Silent version and called it a 'thunk' instead of a 'clack', and HLPLANET's Marcus Richardson called the Phoenix V3 'really quiet'. RTINGS tested the Air75 HE with non-silent Gateron Low-Profile Magnetic Jade Pro switches and keeps its dBA figure behind membership. The page can honestly say the quietness claim is by ear, with 55.1 dBA at 10 cm as the reference for an ordinary magnetic board.

findings.label: Typing loudness of a stock (non-silent) magnetic-switch board, Epomaker HE75 V2 with Creamy Jade switches, measured by Hardware Busters
findings.value: 55.1 dBA average in casual typing; 69.9 dBA peak on heavy spacebar strikes; room 31.9 dBA
findings.source_title: Epomaker HE75 V2 TMR review, Typing Experience & Sound Analysis (Hardware Busters)
findings.note: Review dated 2026-08-07, byline given as Robotronic. CEM DT-8852 Class 2 meter, A-weighted, fast response, 10 cm from the board edge at desk height. The meter's floor is 30 dBA. The HE75 V2 TMR measured within run-to-run variation of the HE75 V2. Not a candidate board; a baseline only. Average minus room: 55.1 − 31.9 = 23.2 dB.

findings.label: Only dBA figure on RTINGS' best quiet keyboards page

findings.label: Phoenix V3 silent magnetic switch force and travel, as listed in HLPLANET's review (Marcus Richardson)
findings.value: 45 ± 5 gf at 2.0 mm; 35 gf minimum initial; 58 gf maximum end force; 3.5 ± 0.2 mm total travel; 95 ± 15 Gs initial and 580 ± 50 Gs bottom flux
findings.source_title: Review: Gamakay Phoenix V3 Silent Magnetic Switch (HLPLANET)
findings.note: Published 2026-07-01. No measurement method is described, so these read as spec-sheet values. The review's 'Sound test' section (done in a Gamakay NS75) is empty; its verdict is 'Really quiet with decent quality', with no dB figure. Mercury V3 in the same table: 55 gf maximum end force.

findings.note: This is the mechanical TK75 V2 with Phoenix V2 (40 gf, 3.3 mm travel), not the Hall effect TK75HE V2 with Phoenix V3. The page showed a 2025-01-18 publish date and a 2026-10-05 update. Relevant only as a named warning that stabilised keys can tick on a silent-switch Gamakay board.
